episodes.165494: An expansive area of stratiform rain with isolated thunderstorms produced localized flooding in portions of far south central Missouri.
episodes.165734: A broken line of thunderstorms moved rapidly east-northeastward during the early morning hours. A few damaging wind events and a weak tornado accompanied the storms. A low amplitude mid-level shortwave trough over the southern Plains ejected northeast into the Ohio Valley, providing support for the broken line of storms. A surface low tracked northeast across Missouri and Illinois. Within the warm sector of this low pressure system, buoyancy was very weak but adequate for thunderstorms. An intense low level jet over 70 knots translated northeast from Arkansas into Kentucky. The very strong winds near the surface contributed to the tornado and wind damage. Pockets of flooding occurred where the most intense storms passed through, mainly in Hickman and Carlisle Counties.
episodes.165738: A broken line of thunderstorms moved rapidly east-northeastward during the early morning hours. A few microbursts accompanied the storms. A low amplitude mid-level shortwave trough over the southern Plains ejected northeast into the Ohio Valley, providing support for the broken line of storms. A surface low tracked northeast across Missouri and Illinois. Within the warm sector of this low pressure system, buoyancy was very weak but adequate for thunderstorms. An intense low level jet over 70 knots translated northeast across Arkansas toward southeast Missouri. The very strong winds near the surface contributed to the microbursts.
episodes.165740: A few thunderstorms formed in the early morning hours February 22nd. Small hail was reported with many storms, and one storm in Rock Island County produced dime size hail.
episodes.165817: Several rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms moved across the region on the 17th. Two to four inches were common, which resulted in isolated flash flooding and more widespread flooding of rivers. The heavy rain occurred ahead of a cold front as it entered southeast Missouri and southern Illinois from the northwest. Weak waves of low pressure moved northeast along the front. A strong 850 mb jet up to 60 to 70 knots was accompanied by a strong surge of warm moist air through the Mississippi River Valley.
episodes.165818: Several rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms moved across the region on the 17th. Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches created pockets of road flooding and then widespread river flooding in subsequent days. The heavy rain occurred ahead of a cold front as it entered southeast Missouri and southern Illinois from the northwest. Weak waves of low pressure moved northeast along the front. A strong 850 mb jet up to 60 to 70 knots was accompanied by a strong surge of warm moist air through the Mississippi River Valley.
episodes.165820: Several rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms moved across the region on the 17th. Rainfall of 3 to 5 inches created pockets of road flooding, along with flash flooding of creeks that affected several dwellings. Larger rivers rose out of their banks in subsequent days. The heavy rain occurred ahead of a cold front as it entered southeast Missouri and southern Illinois from the northwest. Weak waves of low pressure moved northeast along the front. A strong 850 mb jet up to 60 to 70 knots was accompanied by a strong surge of warm moist air through the Mississippi River Valley.
episodes.165976: Warm air spread across the area along with heavy rain and thunderstorms during the early morning of February 22nd.  Some of the thunderstorms produced small hail.  A cold front then moved into northern Illinois bringing freezing rain to far northern Illinois.  The heavy rain caused localized flooding.||Ice accumulation amounts from the freezing rain included 0.15 inches in Woodstock; 0.10 inches at McCullom Lake, Towers Lake, near Lakewood and three miles northeast of Woodstock; 0.09 inches at Waukegan Airport; 0.05 inches at Rockford Airport and 0.01 inches at Chicago Executive Airport.
episodes.166287: A warming trend was noted through Feb 22nd across the state before yet another Arctic airmass moved in from the north. Ahead of the leading cold front, a few severe thunderstorms developed and moved from west central to northeast Arkansas during the early morning hours of Feb 22nd. Mainly wind damage was reported across these areas with some roof damage and numerous trees blown down. Some heavy rain was noted as well, mainly across the northern half of the state. In the wake of the storms, yet another round if winter weather was expected.
episodes.166571: Several rounds of severe storms moved across the region as a strong shortwave and trough moved into the Southern Plains. Most of the hail reports were between 1-1.75 and fell along a line stretching west to east across the northern portions of the DFW Metroplex. A neighborhood in Wise County received substantial damage due to wind driven hail up to the size of golf balls.
episodes.166803: A deep low pressure system drew warm and moist air into western Virginia from the Gulf of Mexico, and produced rounds of light to occasionally moderate rainfall across Smyth County over a 3-day period, with the most substantial rainfall occurring on February 24th.    Rainfall rates were observed approaching 1 inch per hour at times. The rainfall affected mainly the smaller creeks and streams, though multiple stream gauges for the larger rivers of the Holston basin remained within Action Stage and did not leave their banks.  The lack of flooding had much to do with local streamflows measuring below-normal to well below-normal, given the lack of precipitation for several weeks prior to this event.
episodes.166897: A few thunderstorms occurred across southwest Wisconsin during the morning of February 22nd. These storms produced some hail with the largest reported being penny sized near Mount Zion (Crawford County).
episodes.166901: Scattered storms developed during the afternoon and brought hail and damaging winds to portions of central Mississippi.
episodes.166922: During the morning hours, a cold front, which had already produce a tornado, pushed east through central Kentucky. The strongest part of the line only made it as far north as the southern most row of Kentucky counties. This limited central Kentucky storm damage to one report out of Allen County. Most of the damage from the line was in western Kentucky and Tennessee.
episodes.166942: An unseasonably warm and moist airmass pushed into the Mid-South by early morning on February 22, 2022.  A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front producing damaging winds across eastern Arkansas and northwest Tennessee.
episodes.166943: An unseasonably warm and moist airmass pushed into the Mid-South by early morning on February 22, 2022.  A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front producing damaging winds across eastern Arkansas and northwest Tennessee.
episodes.166944: An unseasonably warm and moist airmass pushed into the Mid-South by early morning on February 22, 2022.  A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front producing damaging winds across eastern Arkansas and northwest Tennessee.
episodes.167085: Numerous showers and thunderstorms affected Middle Tennessee on February 22. Some of the storms became severe with a few reports of large hail and wind damage. In addition, heavy rainfall resulted in flooding across several areas of Middle Tennessee. Rainfall totals from February 21 to February 25 ranged from 3 to over 7 inches fell across the area, which led to widespread river flooding on most rivers and streams across the region through the rest of the month.

A National Weather Service damage survey revealed a microburst with estimated peak winds near 90 mph struck south central Butler County. The microburst began just north of Allred Lake Natural Area along County Road 2601 and ended along County Road 214 in Coon Island Conservation Area. The maximum path width was about 1000 yards. A semi and an empty grain bin were both flipped onto their sides. Three wooden electrical poles were pushed nearly to the ground. A grain silo was severely dented. A mobile home was shifted off its foundation, and a small portion of its roof decking was removed. Several outbuildings were severely damaged or destroyed. One brick home suffered wind damage to several of its window sills. A handful of trees were uprooted, and several large tree limbs were broken.
